## 2026-11-17 02:29 · The builder to the lead (SR Leagues lane 2.163: sign-up and sign-in say what is happening)

Builder of 2.163 (lane/2.163-sign-in-says), one question; I carry on with the rest meanwhile.
R-31 ("You already have an account. This changes its password…" on the password screen, after the code) needs the web app to know, after a RIGHT code, whether the address already had an account. Nothing in the SignInService interface says so today: CodeProof is {proof, proofExpiresAt}; the outcome ('password-changed') arrives only after saving. Both adapters already know it at that moment (local: accounts.get(email); Supabase: store.accounts.accountExists(made.user.id), as setPassword works it out).
My brief says I change no adapter. The clean way is additive and tiny: `accountExists: boolean` on CodeProof (sign-in-service.ts), filled in the two verifyCode returns (local-sign-in.ts, supabase-sign-in.ts), with a test in each adapter's tests that it is false for a new address and true for one with an account, and that BEFORE the code nothing changes (T-68). It touches no wiring, no limit, no startup.
The only other way I see without it is an encrypted value in the flow cookie with a key held in the server's memory, which forgets it on a restart: worse.
Unless you answer otherwise, I will build everything else first and do the additive field last, as its own commit, so it is easy to drop or rebase onto 2.93's work.

## 2026-11-17 02:30 · The lead to the builder (SR Leagues lane 2.163: sign-up and sign-in say what is happening)

From the lead, step 2.163, answering your question: YES, the additive field. `accountExists: boolean` on `CodeProof`, filled in the two `verifyCode` returns, with the tests you name (false for a new address, true for one with an account, and BEFORE a right code nothing differs: T-68), as its OWN LAST COMMIT, exactly as you propose; it is known only after the mailbox's owner has proved themselves with the code, so it tells a stranger nothing. No cookie trick. One more thing for your list, found by the reviewer of step 2.157 on the sign-in screen (your files, not that lane's): on the sign-in screen that "Use another account" or a refusal's "Sign in" opens, the link "Back to {league}" leads to the REFUSED address, not to the league: a coach who changes their mind lands on the refusal again, and a visitor sent there from `/{league}/admin` taps it and stays on sign-in. It must lead to the league's home (through the address helper), while signing in still brings the person back to where they were going. Add it with its check. Also for you to know: step 2.157's fix round will send a signed-out person at ANY admin address to sign in and back (today only the admin home and the tracker do): your screens must read rightly for someone who arrives that way. No answer needed.
